page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The system includes 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is supported by a bundled 2458 GB local SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is also robust, showing strong results in large-block read and write memory bandwidth tests. The processor's support for advanced vector extensions (AVX-512) and cryptography instructions (AES, VAES, SHA_NI) contributes to strong performance in extended instruction and encryption tests. Single-core performance and text processing benchmarks fall within the average range.

This server is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, and software compilation, all of which achieved strong benchmark ratings. It is also capable of handling small-to-medium language model inference, though text generation on large 70B models is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25%. Given its high resource density and balanced CPU-to-memory ratio, the D64ds_v5 offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for enterprise workloads requiring local high-speed SSD storage and substantial multi-threaded compute capacity without the need for dedicated GPU acceleration.
